capabilities: Render Markdown checklists as a nested task tree and Kanban board
Derive parent task status from child tasks (roll-up)
Link tasks to their own notes with self-maintaining frontmatter
Track cross-tree dependencies with blocked-path highlighting
Maintain agent instructions (AGENTS.md, Claude Code skill) in the vault
disambiguation: Not just a tree viewer for tasks; it also renders the same checklist as a Kanban board, a project dashboard, and agent-readable files.
extras: Not yet in the community plugin directory; install is via BRAT or manual release download. The repo's docs/ folder doubles as an Obsidian vault with a format spec and example board.
motivation: The author says the point is cognitive clarity rather than features: keeping every node anchored to the big picture while removing the friction of tools that flatten real, non-linear projects.
problem: Real projects nest tasks several levels deep, but most task tools flatten them into a list or allow only one level of nesting, which hides how subtasks hold back milestones.

relations.evidence: The convention deliberately follows the methodology of Google Cloud's Open Knowledge Format (OKF)
Open the vault with Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex and the AI already knows the rules.

summary: Task manager that renders Markdown checklists as a nested task tree and Kanban board with status roll-up, per-task notes, and dependencies.
